title: Streamline kernel loading and dependency pruning for mixed-GPU fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Over the last year we've accumulated multiple ad-hoc kernel discovery and ABI workarounds to support heterogeneous customer fleets (various CUDA, Triton and CUTLASS combinations). This has increased cold-start latency, bloated runtime images, and made upgrades fragile (many of our recent incidents trace to kernel probing/loader behavior).

Goal: Replace the current ad-hoc probing with a two-part approach: 1) a deterministic, versioned runtime ABI surface that narrows compatibility matrix at load-time, and 2) an on-demand lazy kernel loader + pruning pipeline that strips unused kernel variants from deployed images and defers kernel JIT/provision until first-use. This should reduce binary size, improve cold-start for typical workloads, and make CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS upgrades lower-risk.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Median cold-start latency for common gen-text workloads reduced by 18-25% in mixed-GPU pools.
- Deployed runtime image sizes decrease by >=15% for multi-arch artifacts.
- Number of upgrade-time incidents related to kernel ABI probing reduced to 0 for the next two releases.
- Compatibility layer surface documented and test coverage added (unit + integration) for all supported CUDA/Triton combinations.

Design summary:
- Introduce a small, explicit ABI manifest file baked into each runtime artifact listing supported kernel feature variants and the runtime semantic version (ABI v2). Runtimes must expose a quick, deterministic check that fails fast when an incompatible kernel set is present.
- Implement a lazy kernel loader that keeps a tiny bootstrap kernel table and loads larger variant blobs from the image or remote cache on first-use. The loader will run in the GPU process namespace and use a bounded background thread pool to avoid blocking inference threads.
- Add an image prune step in CI that analyzes model graph profiles to keep only the kernel families used by our internal benchmark set (opt-in: customers can request full family retention).
- Provide a compatibility shim that maps a narrow ABI to older kernel symbol names during a 2-release deprecation window. This shim is toggled off by default in runtime-1.20 and enabled via feature flag for canary clusters.

Migration plan and rollout:
1) Feature branch + internal smoke CI for ABI manifest generation and loader (2 weeks).
2) Canary deploy to non-critical dev clusters with shim enabled (runtime-1.20-canary, 1 week).
3) Run workload replay jobs from production traces and compare cold-start and runtime errors (2 weeks).
4) If stable, flip shim off for canary and progressively roll to dedicated pools with staged traffic shifting (4 weeks).
5) Post-rollout: collect telemetry and run upgrade dry-runs against latest customer fleet images for 8 weeks.

Testing and safety nets:
- Unit tests for manifest parser and loader error paths.
- Integration tests that simulate missing kernel blobs, version mismatches and fallback behavior.
- Fuzz-run the manifest to loader interface to catch parsing edge-cases.
- Rollback plan: if increased error rate >1% or latency regressions >10% in canary, automatically revert image and enable legacy shim globally for affected pools.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Missing kernel variants for niche models. Mitigation: opt-in full-family retention and a diagnostic endpoint to request missing kernels at runtime.
- Risk: Remote-on-demand loads add tail latency. Mitigation: bounded prefetch heuristics and local cache with eviction tuned by model access patterns.
- Risk: Buggy shim hides real incompatibilities. Mitigation: monitor detailed compatibility telemetry and fail open for safety-critical customers.

Open design questions:
- Which symbol/versioning scheme do we standardize on for the ABI manifest? (proposal: semantic triple <abi_major>.<cuda_compat>.<cutlass_profile>)
- How do we secure remote kernel blobs for private deployments? (proposal: signed artifacts + KMS-backed envelope encryption for private clusters)

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/ABI-Lazy-Kernel-Design
- Draft PR for manifest format: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1937
- Benchmark dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood.company/d/bench/kernel-loads

Implementation notes: start in runtime/kernel-loader/, keep change small and feature-gated. Coordinate with infra for image build changes and with packaging for new image layout.

2025-11-24 - Benji Morales: Prototype of manifest parser landed in branch eng/abi-manifest. Early microbench shows ~12% cold-start improvement when kernel families are pruned locally. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1937

2025-11-28 - Design review (Charlotte Wu): Reviewed ABI triple proposal; requested explicit mapping table for legacy symbol aliases. Added to design doc. Follow-up: finalize encryption approach for private clusters with Security.
